_comment: Ground truth for the synthetic counting family (#1256, part A of #776): apiary visit notices from the invented Brackenmoor Beekeepers, corpus threads 102-112 (indexer/tests/baseline/corpus.py). Written by hand from the corpus text, never from what search returns. messages classifies every family message: shape is the #776 shape it stands for; notice and report name the distinct visit (the underlying item) the message gives notice of or reports on; deliveries counts the Maildir files that claim the message's Message-ID (2 for the duplicate delivery, so two claimant IDs); folder is set when it is not INBOX or Sent's default scope (Trash). A scenario's expected_messages are the messages of its category outside Trash, trash_messages those in Trash, expected_items the distinct items among expected_messages; trap_terms are the words an agent would look up, each of which must list a decoy while together they reach every expected message. lookups are exact query_messages calls with every matching message ref, repeated once per claimant; make baseline pages each to the end. held_out must equal tests/agent_metrics.py is_held_out(id); held-out scenarios are never used to tune anything. Synthetic data only.

apiary-visit-notices.question: How many apiary visit notices did I get, and for which visits?

hive-visit-reports.question: Did the hive warden send any visit reports, and for which visits?
